fixes.explanation: Right, the text doesn't show Matthew asking for any time. Jesus says, “Follow Me,” and Matthew got up and followed Him (Matthew 9:9). There's no pause in the verse. I think walking away from a tax booth is a big step, and the text just says he got up.

They're a good guess for a big gathering, but the text doesn't put them at this dinner. It says many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Jesus and His disciples. The Pharisees are named in the very next verse, when they see this and ask His disciples a question. Priests and elders aren't on the list.

Not quite. The text says the Pharisees asked His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” It doesn't show them asking Jesus. Then, on hearing this, Jesus answers. Who they ask is right there in the verse, friend.

Right, the question goes to the disciples. The Pharisees asked His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” The text doesn't say they asked Jesus. Then, on hearing this, Jesus answers.

Jesus says, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” It's an easy picture. Somebody who's hurting is the one heading for the doctor's office. The sick are the ones who need the doctor.

Wise sounds nice, but it's not Jesus' word, friend. He says, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” I've seen plenty of smart folks sneeze into their sleeves, so being wise sure doesn't keep you out of the waiting room. The sick are the ones who need the doctor.

Priests don't come up in this line, friend. Jesus says, “For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” That's His answer about who is eating at Matthew's house. The call goes to sinners, and the table was full of them.

Jesus says, “But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.” While the bridegroom is with the guests, they don't mourn. Once He's taken from them, then they will fast. That's the time He means.

Nothing gets called off in what Jesus says. He says, “But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.” The wedding never gets canceled in His words. The bridegroom being taken is the change He names.

Jesus says, “For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.” The patch He means is unshrunk cloth sewn on an old garment. So the fix makes the problem bigger. The hole ends up worse than before.
